issues.author: C. M. v. Bay
issues.description:
## Bug Description

On RDNA4 (Navi 48, RX 9070 XT), the `/sys/class/drm/cardN/device/pp_dpm_mclk` sysfs file does **not** mark the currently active memory clock state with `*` during active 3D rendering. This behaviour differs from RDNA2 (RX 6800 XT), where the active state is always marked.

## pp_dpm_mclk content at idle (correct)

```
0: 96Mhz *
1: 456Mhz 
2: 772Mhz 
3: 875Mhz 
4: 1124Mhz 
5: 1258Mhz 
```

## pp_dpm_mclk content during active 3D load (bug)

```
0: 96Mhz 
1: 456Mhz 
2: 772Mhz 
3: 875Mhz 
4: 1124Mhz 
5: 1258Mhz 
```

No `*` marker on any line during the entire duration of a 3D workload (tested with FurMark). The marker reappears a few seconds after the workload ends.

The hwmon interface correctly reflects the actual memory clock at all times:
```
/sys/class/hwmon/hwmonN/freq2_input  # label: mclk

Returns e.g. `1258000000` (Hz) under load while pp_dpm_mclk shows no `*`.

issues.title: amdgpu (RX 590): GTT memory leak on resume from suspend (partially improved in 6.17 but not fixed)
issues.author: Ricardo Sanz
issues.description:
**Human briefing**

It seems there is a memory leak on resume from suspend, with `/sys/class/drm/card1/device/mem_info_gtt_used` bumping several hundreds megabytes.

`cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/1/amdgpu_evict_gtt` makes the system reduce the mem_info_gtt_used value to around 70MB.

I've tested it with IA help. Kernel 6.17 improved the situation but still happens (just less memory leaked). 

**IA report (reviewed by a human)**

---

---

#### Description

On resume from suspend (S3), the amdgpu driver leaks GTT memory (system RAM pinned for GPU access) that is not released back to the OS. The leak accumulates across sleep/wake cycles and persists until reboot. The kernel must compensate by dropping page cache to keep the system running.

Additionally, each resume cycle permanently fragments the kernel's direct map: 2M page mappings are split into 4K pages (due to write-combined GTT pages), and these splits are never consolidated until reboot.

#### Measurements

**Kernel 6.8.0-117:**

|  | Value |
|--|-------|
| GTT before sleep | 687 MB |
| GTT after wake | 1,823 MB |
| **Leaked per cycle** | **+1,136 MB** |
| DirectMap4k increase per cycle | +260 MB (2M → 4K splits) |

**Kernel 6.17.0-29:**

|  | Value |
|--|-------|
| GTT before sleep | 213 MB |
| GTT after wake | 904 MB |
| **Leaked per cycle** | **+691 MB** |
| DirectMap4k increase per cycle | +260 MB (2M → 4K splits) |

Progress between 6.8 → 6.17: baseline GTT reduced by 474 MB, leak per cycle reduced by 445 MB (\~39%).

A local test patch that treats CH7218 branch ID `0x2B02F0` as a DP-HDMI PCON/converter makes the TV immediately report `4K VRR HDR`.

This may affect CH7218 USB-C DP Alt Mode -> HDMI 2.1 adapters, not only conventional DisplayPort-to-HDMI dongles.

## Suspected affected scope

This appears likely to affect the rarer CH7218-based USB-C to HDMI 2.1 adapters, where the source side is USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode rather than a conventional full-size DisplayPort output.

Most existing CH7218 VRR testing and patch discussion appears to focus on normal DisplayPort-to-HDMI 2.1 adapters/dongles. My device is physically USB-C to HDMI 2.1, while electrically still carrying DisplayPort Alt Mode into the CH7218 PCON.

The suspected issue is that this USB-C/DP-Alt-Mode CH7218 topology exposes the correct CH7218 branch device ID (`0x2B02F0`) but does not get classified by AMDGPU as `DISPLAY_DONGLE_DP_HDMI_CONVERTER`. As a result, the generic dongle-type check rejects the path before the CH7218 allowlist/override can make the PCON VRR path active.

- GPU/APU: AMD Ryzen 6600H / Radeon 660M, Rembrandt
- Adapter: CH7218-based USB-C to HDMI 2.1 adapter
- Display: Samsung Q80T

In gamescope we try to use planes when possible - to that end, different test flips are issued by liftoff to figure out if the current configuration is flippable through planes or not. If not, we fall back to a compositing path. At this point we are trying to get a frame on screen, so time is of the essence.

Currently when the cursor is on screen on Deck, we fall back to compositing for various reasons. This currently seems to involve five test commits prior to falling back from liftoff before we give up, and one after, to confirm we can flip our composited full-screen buffer.

For a sample frame here are the duration of said test commits: 1.32ms, 0.11ms, 0.21ms, 0.08ms, 0.04ms, and 0.16ms for the sixth post-compositing test commit.

These are measured on an otherwise idle Zen2 CPU core, using the 'performance' governor to achieve consistency for the purpose of this report.

This means burning 1.82ms of CPU before we can even be sure we need to composite, which is quite unexpected. The first test commit is consistently 1ms+, but even the other numbers seem high, including 0.16ms for the final single-plane commit that is essentially designed to be a perfect fit for the current mode.

issues.author: johnny0
issues.description:
On Kaveri with UMA > 256MB, UVD gets stuck in a bad state after running parallel jobs.

The first set of parallel jobs may finish as expected.  Successive parallel jobs take progressively longer to complete, printing many of the following warnings to the system log:

```
[drm] Fence fallback timer expired on ring uvd
```

As few as two parallel jobs can trigger the issue; successive serial jobs do not trigger the issue.

~~This issue is **not** seen when when the UMA buffer is configured as 256MB.~~ See: [this comment](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/amd/-/issues/4801#note_3363388)

## System information:

 - Debian 13 Trixie
 - Kernel: 5.15.y, 6.12.y, amd-staging-drm-next
 - Platform: Asus A88X-PRO
 - Kaveri

Tested with various versions of mesa and ffmpeg.

## How to reproduce the issue:

- Set the UMA buffer to something more than 256MB.
- Connect a display to avoid #3851 and boot into the system.
- Generate some known good input files:

```
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=1280x720:r=30:d=10 test-720p30.mp4
```

- Fire off a set of parallel UVD jobs:

```
#!/bin/bash

time parallel --jobs 10 ffmpeg -v warning -hwaccel vaapi -hwaccel_device /dev/dri/renderD128 -i test-720p30.mp4 -f null - \;\# ::: {1..10}
```

- Repeat the same command.  Check the system log for warnings.

issues.author: Cody D'Ambrosio
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

The amdkfd_query_rdma_interface is using the old EXPORT_SYMBOL instead of EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL.

```
/**
 * amdkfd_query_rdma_interface - Return interface (function pointers table) for
 *                               rdma interface
 *
 *
 * \param interace     - OUT: Pointer to interface
 *
 * \return 0 if operation was successful.
 */
int amdkfd_query_rdma_interface(const struct amd_rdma_interface **ops)
{
        *ops  = &rdma_ops;

        return 0;
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL(amdkfd_query_rdma_interface);

issues.title: amdgpu DCN 3.5.1 (Strix Halo): flip_done deadlock on active CRTC caused by zombie DP-1 CRTC from optc35_disable_crtc timeout - all kernels
issues.author: Yury Savilov
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

On Linux 7.0-rc7, the amdgpu display manager deadlocks. `amdgpu_dm_atomic_commit_tail` waits on the `flip_done` fence for CRTC-0 (the active HDMI display), which never signals. kwin_wayland\
immediately begins flooding "Pageflip timed out!" at one message per second; the kernel then emits `[CRTC:417:crtc-0] flip_done timed out`, followed by cascading CONNECTOR and PLANE commit timeouts and repeated vblank wait timeouts from `drm_fb_helper_damage_work`. The Wayland compositor becomes completely unresponsive; the system is only accessible via SSH and requires a hard reboot to recover.

This is a clean kernel regression: 7.0-rc6 ran for 26 hours with zero pageflip/vblank errors on identical hardware, identical mesa (1:26.0.2-1),\
and identical kernel parameters. 7.0-rc7 froze within 4.5 hours on the first screen blank/unblank.

The freeze is reproducible on every boot of 7.0-rc7 by waiting for the screen idle timeout (or manually triggering a blank). It does not require any GPU workload.
